### Problem: Recent Actions {#sec-ds-p5-recent}

::: {.p-statement}
A social network shows a "Recent Actions" field of exactly $n$ posts, numbered $1 \ldots n$ from top to bottom at time $0$. Then $m$ actions arrive, one per second, $t = 1 \ldots m$; action $t$ is on some post $p_t$ with $p_t > n$ (a post outside the initial field), and the same $p_t$ may repeat.

On each action the post $p_t$ is moved to (or inserted at) the **top** of the field; if it was not already in the field, the **bottom** post is pushed out. For every initial post $i \in 1..n$, report the second it is pushed out, or `-1` if it is never pushed out. The input has several test cases; in each, $n, m \le 5\cdot10^4$ and $n < p_t \le n + m$, with the sums of $n$ and of $m$ over all test cases bounded by $5\cdot10^4$. Two test cases from the sample: $n = 5$ with actions $6, 7, 8, 9, 10$ gives `5 4 3 2 1`, and $n = 4$ with actions $5, 9, 9, 5, 7$ gives `-1 5 2 1`.

Source: [CF 1799A · Recent Actions](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/1799/A){.solved rating="800"}
:::

::: {.p-intuition}
Every arriving post has id $> n$, so new posts always sit *above* the surviving initial posts, and the bottom of the field is always the highest-numbered initial post still present. An action evicts someone only when its post is not yet in the field, that is, on the **first** appearance of that id (while initial posts remain, no new post is ever pushed out). So the $k$-th distinct id to arrive evicts initial post $n - k + 1$, at the time it first arrives. Record the first-arrival times (`firsts`); post $i$ is evicted at `firsts[n - i]` if at least $n - i + 1$ distinct ids arrived, else never. The timestamps answer the question without simulating the field.
:::

::: {.p-approach}
1. **Move-to-front simulation.** Keep the field as a list; on each action move or insert the post at the top, popping and recording the bottom post when the field overflows. $O(n)$ per action. This is the model for the stress tests.
2. **First-arrival clock.** Track `seen`; a first-time arrival evicts the bottom surviving initial post (a pointer walking down from $n$) and stamps its time; repeats are skipped (@fig-ds-p5-recent shows why the drain order is fixed). $O(1)$ expected per action.
3. **Arrival-rank formula.** Collect `firsts`, the times of distinct arrivals, in one pass; answer post $i$ with `firsts[n - i]` or `-1`. $O(n + m)$, no field and no pointer.

**Invariant of the clock forms.** After the first $t$ actions, with $d$ distinct ids seen so far, the field holds the $\min(d, n)$ newest distinct ids on top and the initial posts $1..n-d$ below them (none if $d \ge n$), so exactly posts $n, n-1, \ldots, n-d+1$ have been evicted, at the first-arrival times of the distinct ids, in order.
:::

::: {#fig-ds-p5-recent}

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    V.array(ax, p, [7, 6, 1, 2, 3], pointers=[(4, "bottom", "pink")],
            colors={0: "cyan", 1: "cyan", 4: "amber"}, index=False,
            label="field after 6,7: new posts on top, initial posts drain from the bottom")
V.show(draw)
```

After arrivals $6$ then $7$ (both $>n$), posts $5$ and $4$ have been pushed out at seconds $1$ and $2$. The amber bottom `3` is the next initial post to go; new posts never sit below a surviving initial post, which is why the drain order is exact.

:::

The buttons are in order. Each one keeps the previous solution and changes only what that form changes.

::: {.panel-tabset .solution-forms}

#### Move-to-front simulation

::: {.form-next}
Build the field verbatim. `if p in field: move to top (no eviction) else: pop bottom (record its time) and prepend`. $O(n)$ per action because of the membership search and shift — the baseline.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("recent", "simulate")
    assert str(final) == "[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
class RecentSim:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.field = list(range(1, n + 1))   # top .. bottom
        self.evict = {}
        self.t = 0

    def action(self, p):
        self.t += 1
        if p in self.field:
            self.field.remove(p)
            self.field.insert(0, p)          # already shown: reorder, nobody leaves
        else:
            gone = self.field.pop()          # bottom is pushed out
            self.evict[gone] = self.t
            self.field.insert(0, p)

    def result(self, n):
        return [self.evict.get(i, -1) for i in range(1, n + 1)]


s = RecentSim(5)
for p in [6, 7, 8, 9, 10]:
    s.action(p)
assert s.result(5) == [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
s = RecentSim(4)
for p in [5, 9, 9, 5, 7]:
    s.action(p)
assert s.result(4) == [-1, 5, 2, 1]
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<int> recentSim(int n, const vector<int>& p) {
    list<int> field; vector<int> evict(n + 1, -1);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) field.push_back(i);
    for (int t = 0; t < (int)p.size(); ++t) {
        int x = p[t];
        auto it = find(field.begin(), field.end(), x);
        if (it != field.end()) field.erase(it);
        else { evict[field.back()] = t + 1; field.pop_back(); }
        field.push_front(x);
    }
    vector<int> ans; for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) ans.push_back(evict[i]);
    return ans;
}
```
:::

#### First-arrival clock

::: {.form-next}
Because every arrival id is $> n$, a first-time arrival always evicts the lowest surviving **initial** post. Walk a pointer `nxt` down from $n$; on the first sighting of a post stamp `evict[nxt] = t` and decrement; skip repeats. $O(1)$ per action.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("recent", "firstarr")
    assert str(final) == "[5, 4, 3, 2, 1]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
class RecentFirstArr:
    def __init__(self, n):
        self.n = n

    def solve(self, p):
        seen = set()
        evict = {}
        nxt = self.n
        for t, x in enumerate(p, 1):
            if x in seen:                 # a repeat only reorders: no eviction
                continue
            seen.add(x)
            if nxt >= 1:                  # evict the lowest surviving initial post
                evict[nxt] = t
                nxt -= 1
        return [evict.get(i, -1) for i in range(1, self.n + 1)]


assert RecentFirstArr(5).solve([6, 7, 8, 9, 10]) == [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
assert RecentFirstArr(4).solve([5, 9, 9, 5, 7]) == [-1, 5, 2, 1]
# agree with the simulation on valid inputs (arrival ids all > n)
for _ in range(300):
    n = random.randint(1, 6)
    m = random.randint(1, 12)
    p = [n + random.randint(1, 6) for _ in range(m)]
    s = RecentSim(n)
    for x in p:
        s.action(x)
    assert s.result(n) == RecentFirstArr(n).solve(p)
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<int> recentFirstArr(int n, const vector<int>& p) {
    unordered_set<int> seen; vector<int> ans(n + 1, -1); int nxt = n;
    for (int t = 0; t < (int)p.size(); ++t) {
        if (seen.count(p[t])) continue;
        seen.insert(p[t]);
        if (nxt >= 1) ans[nxt] = t + 1, --nxt;
    }
    ans.erase(ans.begin()); return ans;
}
```
:::

#### Arrival-rank formula

::: {.form-next}
The two-loop submission: one pass to record the first-arrival time of each distinct post (`firsts`), then post $i$ is evicted by the $(n-i+1)$-th such arrival. No field, no pointer walk — just an index into `firsts`, or $-1$ when too few arrivals happened.
:::

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| renderings: [light, dark]
def draw(ax, p):
    title, inp, steps, final = Traces.get("recent", "formula")
    assert str(final) == "[-1, 5, 2, 1]"
    V.story(ax, p, title, inp, steps, final)
V.show(draw)
```

::: {.panel-tabset group="lang"}

##### Python

```{python}
def recent_formula(n, p):
    firsts = []
    seen = set()
    for t, x in enumerate(p, 1):
        if x not in seen:                 # arrival ids are > n, so each first one evicts
            seen.add(x)
            firsts.append(t)
    ans = []
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        k = n - i                          # post n dies on arrival #1, post 1 on arrival #n
        ans.append(firsts[k] if k < len(firsts) else -1)
    return ans


assert recent_formula(5, [6, 7, 8, 9, 10]) == [5, 4, 3, 2, 1]
assert recent_formula(4, [5, 9, 9, 5, 7]) == [-1, 5, 2, 1]
# cross-check the formula against the simulation on valid inputs
for _ in range(300):
    n = random.randint(1, 7)
    p = [n + random.randint(1, 8) for _ in range(random.randint(1, 15))]
    s = RecentSim(n)
    for x in p:
        s.action(x)
    assert recent_formula(n, p) == s.result(n)
```

##### C++

```cpp
vector<int> recentFormula(int n, const vector<int>& p) {
    vector<int> firsts; unordered_set<int> seen;
    for (int t = 0; t < (int)p.size(); ++t)
        if (!seen.count(p[t])) { seen.insert(p[t]); firsts.push_back(t + 1); }
    vector<int> ans(n, -1);
    for (int i = 1; i <= n; ++i) {
        int k = n - i;
        if (k < (int)firsts.size()) ans[i - 1] = firsts[k];
    }
    return ans;
}
```
:::

:::

::: {.p-complexity}
**Move-to-front simulation:** $O(n)$ per action (the membership search and the shift), $O(nm)$ in total; $O(n)$ space for the field. **First-arrival clock:** $O(1)$ expected per action (one hash-set lookup), $O(n + m)$ in total; $O(m)$ space for `seen`. **Arrival-rank formula:** $O(n + m)$ in total, one pass over the actions and one over the posts; $O(m)$ space for `seen` and `firsts`, plus $O(n)$ for the answer.
:::

::: {.p-edge}
- **Fewer distinct arrivals than posts**: if $|firsts| < n$, the surviving initial posts (indices $1 \ldots n-|firsts|$) answer $-1$; the `k < len(firsts)` guard handles it without a special case.
- **A repeat of an already-shown post** reorders the top but evicts nobody — counting it as an arrival would wrongly kill an extra initial post.
- **The drain direction**: post $n$ (bottom) leaves on the first distinct arrival, post $1$ on the $n$-th — the index $k = n - i$ encodes "from the back," matching that the field pushes out its tail.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Common mistakes"}
- **Simulating the array order** to answer and paying $O(n)$ per action, when only the *count of distinct arrivals* and their *times* matter. The field's internal order is irrelevant to the initial posts' fates.
- **Off-by-one on the arrival rank**: post $i$ maps to `firsts[n-i]`, not `firsts[i]`; the bottom post dies first.
- **Worrying about a new post that is pushed out and comes back.** A new post can only reach the bottom after all initial posts are gone, and from then on the initial posts' answers are fixed; so `seen` never needs to forget anything.
:::

**Variants.** When arriving ids may also be initial posts ($p_t \le n$), an initial post can be moved back to the top and the drain order is no longer fixed; then the field must really be simulated, with a linked list plus a `post -> node` map for $O(1)$ moves.

::: {.practice}
- [CF 500C · New Year Book Reading](https://codeforces.com/problemset/problem/500/C){rating="1600"} — a move-to-front stack of books where the cost of each read is the weight above the book; simulate it, then notice that the first-read order fixes the initial stack.
:::
